              "question": "Over the course of events, do the stakes remain confined to a single domain, or expand from personal to wider social/cosmic domains?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "confined_to_single_domain",
                "expand_from_personal_to_social_or_institutional",
                "expand_to_cosmic_or_existential_scope",
                "contract_from_broad_to_intimate"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Compare early and late stakes: if the story starts and ends with the same domain (e.g., internal grief only), classify as confined; if it grows from individual to community/institution (e.g., riots, reforms), or even to world/ontology-threatening stakes, code the appropriate expansion; if it begins with large-scale stakes and narrows to private resolution, choose contract_from_broad_to_intimate."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_TYP_008",
              "name": "Event-time coverage of the main arc",
              "question": "What is the primary length of story-world time covered by the main event sequence (excluding brief prologues/epilogues)?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "single_scene_or_few_hours",
                "single_day_and_night",
                "several_days_to_months",
                "multiple_years",
                "nonlinear_or_deep_time_spanning_generations_or_epochs"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Track explicit or implied time markers across the core narrative (not counting very short framing devices); choose the category that best matches the elapsed in-world duration between earliest and latest central events.",
              "merged_from": [
                "TMP_DUR_001"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "schemas_and_arc": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrative Schemas and Global Arc",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_004",
              "name": "Mode of resolution of the main event chain",
              "question": "How is the central conflict or event chain brought to a close, if at all?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "resolved_through_external_action_or_intervention",
                "resolved_through_internal_understanding_or_acceptance",
                "partial_or_compromise_resolution",
                "open_or_ambiguously_unresolved",
                "catastrophic_or_irrevocably_negative_outcome"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify the final events addressing the core conflict; code whether they involve decisive external acts (escape, arrest, coup), an internal shift (forgiveness, letting go, insight), a negotiated or mixed outcome, a deliberately open ending with no clear outcome, or an outcome framed as catastrophic (death, collapse, unrepaired devastation).",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_SCH_005",
                "EVT_SCH_015",
                "PLT_CON_006",
                "PLT_CON_005"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "narrative_schemas_and_arc": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrative Schemas, Arc Shape, and Resolution",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_002",
              "name": "Arc Completeness Relative to Implied Plot",
              "question": "How much of the implied full plot does the text actually cover?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "setup_only_or_preliminary_phase",
                "partial_arc_with_cliffhanger_or_open_crisis",
                "full_arc_to_local_resolution",
                "multi_phase_arc_extending_well_beyond_prompt"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Judge whether the story stops early (ending before main conflict escalates), ends amid crisis, carries through to a clear resolution of central conflict, or additionally follows long aftermath/epilogue phases."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_003",
              "name": "Strength of Event Escalation",
              "question": "How strongly do events escalate in stakes or intensity over the course of the narrative?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1_almost_flat_little_or_no_escalation",
                "2_mild_escalation",
                "3_moderate_escalation",
                "4_strong_escalation",
                "5_relentless_or_steep_escalation"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Track how risk, scale of consequences, or emotional intensity change from beginning to end. Map to a 1\u20135 rating where higher scores show a clear, engineered ramp-up toward crisis."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_006",
              "name": "Use of Explicit Frame Narrative",
              "question": "Does the story use an explicit frame (e.g., a narrator in the present recounting past events to an audience)?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "no_frame_or_minimal_metacommentary",
                "has_explicit_frame_story_or_recounting_context"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Check opening and closing: is there a recognizable outer situation (interview, letter, tavern conversation, counseling session) within which the main events are told as memory or tale?",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_SCH_012",
                "PLT_STR_004",
                "PLT_STR_008",
                "TMP_ORD_003"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_008",
              "name": "Dominant Event Initiation Source",
              "question": "What primarily triggers new major events across the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "character_choice_and_desire",
                "external_forces_or_accidents",
                "institutional_or_task_driven_demands",
                "supernatural_or_technological_intrusion",
                "gradual_situational_drift_without_clear_incidents"
              ],
              "detection_method": "For each major plot turn, code its initiating cause: deliberate decisions, chance/disaster, orders/assignments/protocols, magical/alien devices, or slow incremental change; then select the overall dominant category.",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_CAU_009"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "causal_connectivity": {
          "aspect_name": "Causal Structure and Connectivity",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_001",
              "name": "Explicitness of causal links",
              "question": "How explicitly does the narration mark cause-and-effect relations between events?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "predominantly_explicit_causation",
                "mixed_explicit_and_implicit",
                "predominantly_implicit_or_inferred",
                "weak_or_non_causal_associative_sequence"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Examine transitions between major events: frequent use of clear connectors ('because', 'so that', 'therefore', explicit causal commentary) indicates predominantly_explicit_causation; if many links must be inferred or are left ambiguous, classify accordingly; if scenes feel merely juxtaposed by theme or mood without causal necessity, choose weak_or_non_causal_associative_sequence.",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_CAU_007"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_002",
              "name": "Continuity of the main causal chain",
              "question": "To what extent does a single, continuous causal chain carry through from inciting incident to ending, versus multiple disjoint or restarting chains?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                1,
                2,
                3,
                4,
                5
              ],
              "detection_method": "Trace how often later events are direct or indirect consequences of prior ones in the same line of action; score 1 if the story is largely episodic with unrelated episodes, 3 if there is a discernible but occasionally broken chain, 5 if nearly every significant event is tightly linked in one continuous line of cause-and-effect."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_003",
              "name": "Attention to unintended consequences",
              "question": "Does the story foreground downstream, unintended consequences of characters' actions as significant events?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "no_salient_unintended_consequences",
                "prominent_unintended_consequences"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for explicit event sequences where an action aimed at X results in Y or Z instead (or in addition), and where these side-effects receive narrative weight (e.g., riots after a scientific demo, institutional reforms after a confession); mark prominent if such chains are central rather than incidental."
            }
          ]
        },
        "causal_dynamics": {
          "aspect_name": "Causal Structure and Event Connectivity",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_004",
              "name": "Perceived Determinism of Outcomes",
              "question": "Does the narrative present outcomes as fated/inevitable, contingent, or somewhere in between?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "strongly_fated_or_inevitable",
                "mixed_fate_and_contingency",
                "highly_contingent_or_random_feeling"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Note explicit prophecies, fatalism, or 'could not have been otherwise' narration versus coin flips, arbitrary accidents, or emphasized chance; classify according to overall tone about inevitability."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_005",
              "name": "Primary Agent of Causal Momentum",
              "question": "Whose actions most strongly drive the causal chain of the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "protagonist_or_focal_character_driven",
                "antagonist_or_opposing_character_driven",
                "system_environment_or_institution_driven",
                "balanced_or_shifting_among_multiple_agents"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify whether most major turns arise from the main character's choices, from an opponent's initiatives, from impersonal systems (courts, weather, AI, magic), or from several parties in roughly equal measure."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_006",
              "name": "Treatment of Alternative or Repeated Event Paths",
              "question": "How does the story handle multiple versions or repetitions of similar events?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_linear_history_no_alternatives",
                "explicit_multiple_versions_or_branches_of_events",
                "loops_or_resets_of_the_same_event_sequence",
                "ritual_repetition_of_a_template_event_with_variation"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Check whether the narrative offers only one canonical sequence, presents several incompatible accounts (e.g., variant execution reports), replays a loop with resets, or iterates a ritual template (e.g., many similar sieges or tests) as structuring device."
            }
          ]
        },
        "temporal_structure": {
          "aspect_name": "Temporal Arrangement of Events",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_TYP_009",
              "name": "Balance of present-time versus flashback events",
              "question": "Relative to the story's discourse time, are most events shown in present progression, in analeptic flashback, or in a balanced alternation?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "mostly_present_progression",
                "balanced_present_and_past",
                "mostly_past_or_recollected_events"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess whether the bulk of narrated events unfold along a forward-moving present timeline, whether the text frequently and substantially shifts into past events (memories, case histories) that occupy similar space as the present, or whether the narrative is largely a retrospective recounting with minimal present-time action."
            }
          ]
        },
        "causality": {
          "aspect_name": "Causal Structure & Initiation",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_008",
              "name": "Primary Progression Logic",
              "question": "What is the primary logic by which events are ordered and connected?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "strict_cause_effect",
                "chronological_sequence",
                "associative_thematic",
                "nonlinear_fragmented"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess whether each event is mainly presented as caused by previous ones (strict_cause_effect), simply following in time without strong causal emphasis (chronological_sequence), linked by analogy, motif, or theme more than time (associative_thematic), or arranged in jumps, flashbacks, alternate versions without a single linear through-line (nonlinear_fragmented)."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_018",
              "name": "Use of Repetition or Variants as Event Engine",
              "question": "Does the narrative construct multiple alternative or repeated versions of essentially the same core event (e.g., executions, loops, trial iterations) as a structural device?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "yes",
                "no"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for structurally parallel episodes where the same basic event (an execution, a last meal, a killing, a shopping day, a test) is replayed with variations across sections, letters, or loops. If such patterned repetition is central, mark 'yes'; otherwise 'no'."
            }
          ]
        },
        "temporality_novelty": {
          "aspect_name": "Temporal Handling & Event Novelty",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_016",
              "name": "Temporal Scope of Events",
              "question": "Over what span of story-time do the narrated events mainly extend?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "hours_to_days",
                "weeks_to_months",
                "years",
                "multi_decade/generational",
                "timeless/ahistorical"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Use explicit dates, time references, aging, and contextual clues to infer whether the primary event sequence unfolds across hours/days, weeks/months, years, multiple decades/generations, or in a way that is essentially unmoored from concrete time.",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_TYP_005",
                "SET_TIM_008",
                "SOC_STR_015"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_CAU_017",
              "name": "Event Novelty Orientation",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how strongly does the story lean on surprising, schema-breaking events versus familiar, predictable ones (1 = very predictable, 5 = highly surprising)?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Compare the main turns to genre and archetypal expectations (e.g., quest, mystery, romance). If developments follow well-known patterns with few shocks, choose a low value; if key events repeatedly overturn plausible hypotheses or genre norms, choose a high value."
            }
          ]
        },
        "schema_progression": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrative Schemas & Structural Completeness",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_010",
              "name": "Global Narrative Schema",
              "question": "Which high-level narrative schemas are structurally central to the story?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "quest/journey",
                "investigation/mystery",
                "transformation/redemption",
                "siege/ordeal",
                "slice_of_life",
                "trial/test/game",
                "heist/caper",
                "frame_confession/memoir"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Abstract the plot into patterns: movement toward a goal across space (quest/journey); reconstructing a past event or truth (investigation/mystery); sustained internal change (transformation/redemption); prolonged pressure under threat (siege/ordeal); low-stakes everyday flow without strong arc (slice_of_life); structured challenges, contests, or bargains (trial/test/game); planning and executing a theft or con (heist/caper); or a present-time tale that mainly consists of someone telling about their past (frame_confession/memoir). Select all that clearly apply.",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_SCH_001"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_011",
              "name": "Structural Completeness of Event Arc",
              "question": "How much of a full dramatic arc (setup\u2013rising action\u2013climax\u2013resolution) does the story actually stage?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "setup_only",
                "partial_arc",
                "full_arc_with_resolution"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify whether the text stops after establishing situation and stakes (setup_only), proceeds through conflict and a high point but ends before consequences settle (partial_arc), or carries through to a new equilibrium or explicit aftermath (full_arc_with_resolution)."
            }
          ]
        },
        "escalation_resolution": {
          "aspect_name": "Escalation, Climax, and Resolution",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_013",
              "name": "Tension Escalation Pattern",
              "question": "What overall pattern best describes how stakes and intensity of events evolve across the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "rising_tension_to_climax",
                "episodic_peaks",
                "flat_low_tension",
                "anti_climactic/deflationary"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Track perceived stakes scene by scene. A single broad rise toward a peak is rising_tension_to_climax; several self-contained mini-arcs with their own peaks indicate episodic_peaks; narration that stays at similar, modest stakes is flat_low_tension; if apparent build-ups are regularly undercut or the story seems to avoid climax deliberately, choose anti_climactic/deflationary."
            },
            {
              "id": "EVT_SCH_014",
              "name": "Clear Single Climactic Event",
              "question": "Is there a single, clearly foregrounded climactic event that the narrative unmistakably builds toward?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "yes",
                "no"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Judge whether one particular scene or event is framed as the culmination of prior build-up (through foreshadowing, pacing slowdown, heightened description, or characters' explicit anticipation). If multiple peaks feel of equal weight or there is no pronounced peak, answer 'no'."
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    "perspective": {
      "dimension_name": "Perspective",
      "dimension_description": "Narration: point of view, focalization, dialogue, narrative voice, interior access",
      "aspects": {
        "narrative_person_and_narrator": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrative Person and Narrator",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_POV_001",
              "name": "Dominant narrative person",
              "question": "What is the primary grammatical person used by the main narrator across the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "first_person",
                "second_person",
                "third_person",
                "mixed_no_dominant"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify the default pronoun/verb alignment in narrative (not dialogue): 'I/we' for first, 'you' addressing protagonist for second, 'he/she/they' for third. If substantial sections in different persons without a clear majority, mark 'mixed_no_dominant'.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PER_POV_002"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_POV_007",
              "name": "Embedded documents as narrative voices",
              "question": "Does the story incorporate letters, logs, transcripts, articles, or similar documents as significant alternate narrative channels?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "present",
                "absent"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Scan for typographically or structurally distinct blocks labeled or framed as letters, diary entries, case files, interviews, news clippings, etc. If such documents occupy substantial space and carry their own perspective (not just one-off quotes), mark 'present'; otherwise 'absent'.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PLT_STR_014"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_POV_008",
              "name": "Degree of heteroglossia and polyphony",
              "question": "How many distinct sociolects, registers, or idiolects does the narrative meaningfully orchestrate?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                1,
                2,
                3,
                4,
                5
              ],
              "detection_method": "Count how many clearly differentiated styles of speech or narration appear (e.g., bureaucratic memos, teenage slang, legal language, religious homily, AI system logs). 1 = largely a single uniform register; 3 = several recurring, distinguishable voices or sociolects; 5 = many strongly marked, interacting linguistic registers. Choose an integer based on this rough scale."
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_POV_009",
              "name": "Frequency of direct address to the reader",
              "question": "How often does the text directly address the reader ('you') as an addressee outside the story?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "never",
                "occasional_asides",
                "frequent_or_structural"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify vocative moments where the narrator speaks to an implied reader ('you may think', 'dear reader', 'let me tell you'). If absent, mark 'never'. If they appear a few times as stylistic flourishes, 'occasional_asides'. If this mode is pervasive or structurally central (e.g., 2nd-person essay voice), choose 'frequent_or_structural'.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SIT_MET_015"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "narrative_person_and_configuration": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrative Person and Configuration",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_POV_003",
              "name": "Narrator's diegetic status",
              "question": "What is the narrator's relationship to the story world: are they a protagonist, a minor participant, an external observer, or a collective/institutional voice?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "autodiegetic_protagonist",
                "homodiegetic_minor_character",
                "heterodiegetic_external",
                "collective_or_institutional_voice"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Ask whether the 'I' (if any) is also the central character (autodiegetic) or a side character (homodiegetic). If no narrator-character exists and the voice stands outside the events, mark heterodiegetic_external. If the voice speaks as 'we' for a group, bureaucracy, AI, or community, mark collective_or_institutional_voice.",
              "merged_from": [
                "AGENT_ID_006"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "focalization_depth_and_breadth": {
          "aspect_name": "Focalization Depth and Breadth",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_001",
              "name": "Depth of interior access to characters",
              "question": "How deep into characters' inner life does the non-dialogue narration regularly go?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "On a 1\u20135 scale: 1 = purely external behavior and speech, no thoughts or feelings rendered; 2 = occasional simple feeling labels ('she was angry'); 3 = regular access to thoughts and emotions in sentences paraphrasing them; 4 = sustained, detailed interior monologue or blended narration; 5 = immersive stream-of-consciousness or heavily merged narrator/character voice. Rate based on the dominant practice across the text."
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_002",
              "name": "Breadth of focalization across characters",
              "question": "Across the story, how many distinct characters' inner experiences does the narration give direct access to?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_focal_character",
                "dual_focal_characters",
                "multiple_small_set_3_to_5",
                "many_or_godseye"
              ],
              "detection_method": "List all characters whose thoughts or felt experience are directly rendered (beyond the narrator reporting guesses). Count distinct centers: 1 = single_focal_character; 2 = dual_focal_characters; 3\u20135 distinct minds = multiple_small_set_3_to_5; more than 5 or a sense of generalised human minds = many_or_godseye."
            }
          ]
        },
        "focalization_and_interiority": {
          "aspect_name": "Focalization and Interiority",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_003",
              "name": "Narrative distance (closeness of narrative voice to focalizer)",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how close is the narrating voice to the focalizing consciousness in tone and access?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                1,
                2,
                3,
                4,
                5
              ],
              "detection_method": "1 = extremely intimate, often merging with the character's diction and perceptions; 3 = balanced mix of internal access and external summary, with some narrator phrasing distinct from the character; 5 = distant, reportorial, with little sense of inhabiting any one mind. Judge by how often the narration seems to share the character's idiom and subjectivity versus standing apart."
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_005",
              "name": "Intensity of free indirect discourse",
              "question": "To what extent does the narration rely on free indirect discourse (especially in third person) to convey character consciousness?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "0_none",
                "1_rare_or_isolated_instances",
                "2_moderate_recurring_use",
                "3_frequent_dominant_narrative_mode"
              ],
              "detection_method": "In third-person sections, look for sentences where the diction, exclamations, or evaluative terms clearly match a character's voice but are not marked as quoted thought; estimate how often this occurs relative to total narration and choose the appropriate level.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PER_FOC_006"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "narrator_stance_and_reliability": {
          "aspect_name": "Narrator presence, reliability, and self-awareness",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_007",
              "name": "Narrator reliability",
              "question": "How is the narrator's reliability presented?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "reliable_or_neutral_reporter",
                "explicitly_unreliable_or_deceptive",
                "ambiguous_or_contested_reliability"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for signals such as narrator contradictions, admitted lies, other characters disputing the narration, or obvious gaps; choose 'explicitly_unreliable' when the text foregrounds misreporting, 'ambiguous' when there are subtle reasons to doubt, and 'reliable' when the narrator seems transparent and unchallenged.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PER_POV_004",
                "PLT_STR_013"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_008",
              "name": "Narrator presence/visibility",
              "question": "How visible is the narrator as a distinct speaking presence (with opinions, personality, or direct address)?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1_almost_invisible_narrator_minimal_intrusion",
                "2_rare_asides_or_stylistic_flourishes",
                "3_moderately_present_with_recurring_comments",
                "4_strongly_personalized_voice_guiding_interpretation",
                "5_highly_intrusive_narrator_almost_a_character_in_its_own_right"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess how often the narration steps out of neutral reporting to offer opinions, jokes, generalized statements, or address to the reader; judge the overall prominence of that voice and assign a level from invisible (1) to dominating (5).",
              "merged_from": [
                "PER_FOC_004"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_FOC_009",
              "name": "Degree of explicit evaluative or moral commentary",
              "question": "How frequently does the narrative voice supply explicit moral, ethical, or evaluative commentary on characters and events?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1_none_or_very_subtle_value_judgments",
                "2_occasional_overt_moral_or_evaluative_comments",
                "3_regular_value_judgments_but_not_overwhelming",
                "4_frequent_moralizing_or_didactic_passages",
                "5_morally_commentative_voice_dominates_the_narration"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Note instances where the narrator states that actions are right, wrong, foolish, admirable, or draws explicit morals; count their prevalence across the text and rate from 1 (almost never) to 5 (near-constant framing).",
              "merged_from": [
                "PLT_MOR_005",
                "SIT_MET_502",
                "AGENT_ATTR_023"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "dialogue_usage_and_style": {
          "aspect_name": "Dialogue proportion, function, and style",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_DIA_001",
              "name": "Dialogue-to-narration proportion",
              "question": "Roughly what proportion of the text consists of direct dialogue (quoted speech) versus narration and description?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1_almost_no_dialogue_mostly_narration",
                "2_dialogue_is_rare_but_present",
                "3_balanced_mix_of_dialogue_and_narration",
                "4_dialogue_is_frequent_with_some_narrative_linking",
                "5_dialogue_dominates_with_minimal_narrative_exposition"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Visually scan pages or sections and estimate the fraction of lines that are within dialogue markers versus those that are narrative; assign the closest category from nearly none (1) to almost all (5)."
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_DIA_002",
              "name": "Dialogue tagging style",
              "question": "How are speakers identified and managed in dialogue passages?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "standard_speech_tags_and_action_beats",
                "sparse_or_minimal_tagging_relying_on_voice_or_turn_taking",
                "experimental_or_ambiguous_tagging_with_unattributed_lines"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Examine dialogue sections for attribution patterns; choose 'standard' when most lines have 'he said/she said' or clear beats, 'sparse' when tags are rare but speakers remain inferable, and 'experimental' when multiple lines are left unattributed or tags are unconventional, causing deliberate ambiguity.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PER_DIA_004"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_DIA_003",
              "name": "Primary functions of dialogue",
              "question": "What main functions does dialogue serve in the story?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "advance_plot_or_deliver_crucial_information",
                "reveal_character_psychology_or_relationships",
                "worldbuilding_or_background_exposition",
                "philosophical_or_thematic_debate",
                "comic_relief_or_tone_coloration"
              ],
              "detection_method": "For key dialogue scenes, identify what changes as a result (plot developments, revelations about character, exposition, thematic arguments, jokes); select each function that is consistently prominent across the text."
            },
            {
              "id": "PER_DIA_006",
              "name": "Use of alternative dialogue-like forms",
              "question": "Does the text incorporate dialogue-like communication in alternative formats (such as chat logs, transcripts, forum posts, letters, or reports) that function as conversation?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "yes",
                "no"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for formatted blocks like emails, forum threads, interview transcripts, text-message exchanges, or epistolary sections where turn-taking resembles dialogue; mark 'yes' if such forms are structurally significant rather than incidental."
            }
          ]
        },
        "dialogue_style_and_attribution": {
          "aspect_name": "Dialogue Style and Attribution",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PER_DIA_005",
              "name": "Balance of direct versus indirect speech",
              "question": "Does the story mainly present speech as direct quotations, as indirect/reported speech, or mostly summarize conversation?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "primarily_direct_quoted_speech",
                "mixed_direct_and_indirect_speech",
                "primarily_indirect_or_summary_of_speech"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Scan for quotation-marked lines versus paraphrases ('he told her that...') and summary statements ('they talked about old times'). If most exchanges are quoted verbatim, choose primarily_direct_quoted_speech. If there is a substantial mix of quoted and reported speech, choose mixed_direct_and_indirect_speech. If conversations are seldom quoted and mostly summarized or paraphrased, choose primarily_indirect_or_summary_of_speech."
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    "plot": {
      "dimension_name": "Plot",
      "dimension_description": "Story structure: themes, conflicts, arcs, resolutions, moral content, narrative architecture",
      "aspects": {
        "thematic_architecture": {
          "aspect_name": "Thematic Architecture",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_001",
              "name": "Number of Central Themes",
              "question": "How many distinct central themes does the story develop in a sustained way?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_central_theme",
                "two_primary_themes",
                "multiple_disparate_themes"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify the major abstract concerns (e.g., grief, power, identity, faith) that recur across scenes and drive character decisions. Count how many are treated as co-equal through-line ideas rather than passing motifs."
            }
          ]
        },
        "thematic_structure": {
          "aspect_name": "Thematic Structure and Unity",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_004",
              "name": "Thematic Domains",
              "question": "Which thematic domains are centrally explored in the story's plot?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "survival/fear",
                "power/authority",
                "justice/injustice",
                "love/attachment",
                "identity/selfhood",
                "family/generation",
                "faith/spirituality",
                "class/economics",
                "technology/science",
                "nature/environment",
                "art/creativity",
                "grief/loss",
                "guilt/redemption",
                "violence/trauma",
                "social systems/institutions"
              ],
              "detection_method": "For each listed domain, check whether the plot significantly turns on that concern (e.g., life-or-death survival decisions, class tensions driving events). Select all that clearly shape the main conflicts and resolutions."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_005",
              "name": "Thematic Resolution Pattern",
              "question": "By the end, how are the main thematic tensions treated?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "resolved (tensions largely settled or answered)",
                "partially_resolved (some progress but key tensions remain)",
                "unresolved (tensions deliberately left open)",
                "reframed/transcended (tension transformed into new understanding)"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Compare the initial thematic questions/conflicts to the ending. Decide whether the story closes them down, makes limited headway, leaves them open, or shifts them into a different framing."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_006",
              "name": "Dominant Narrative Archetype",
              "question": "Which classic narrative archetype best fits the story's main arc?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "quest/journey",
                "voyage_and_return",
                "rags_to_riches_or_education",
                "rebirth/redemption",
                "tragedy/fall_from_grace",
                "overcoming_the_monster/disaster",
                "comedy_of_errors/social_farse",
                "investigation/mystery",
                "coming_of_age/initiation",
                "frame_confession_or_testimony",
                "slice_of_life/vignette"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Abstract the core movement of the plot (what the protagonist does and how it ends). Match this to the closest archetype description based on common story patterns."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_007",
              "name": "Archetype Blending",
              "question": "Does the story clearly blend multiple recognizable archetypes?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "no (mostly single archetype)",
                "yes (two or more archetypes substantially combined)"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Decide whether the plot can be cleanly described by one archetype, or whether it equally develops two or more (e.g., an investigation that is also a coming-of-age and a tragedy)."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_008",
              "name": "Thematic Unity",
              "question": "To what extent do subplots, set-pieces, and stylistic flourishes serve a central thematic concern?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Rate 1 if many sequences feel ornamental or unrelated to any central idea; 5 if nearly every scene, subplot, and image clearly reinforces or complicates the same thematic core."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_009",
              "name": "Integration of Subplots with Theme",
              "question": "If subplots exist, how directly do they echo or complicate the central theme?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "no_subplots",
                "directly_thematically_parallel",
                "thematically_contrasting/ironic",
                "largely_thematically_independent"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify any secondary plotlines. Judge whether they mirror the main theme, provide a deliberate counterpoint, or mostly concern different issues."
            }
          ]
        },
        "themes": {
          "aspect_name": "Thematic Structure",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_THM_003",
              "name": "Abstract vs Concrete Thematic Orientation",
              "question": "Are the dominant themes primarily about concrete social/material issues, inner psychology, metaphysical/cosmic questions, or a balanced mix?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "concrete_social",
                "psychological",
                "metaphysical_cosmic",
                "balanced_mix"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Classify the main themes by their level: concrete-social if they focus on institutions, class, law, economics, or specific historical conditions; psychological if focused on identity, desire, trauma, or interpersonal attachment more than external structures; metaphysical/cosmic if they address time, reality, gods, fate, or ontological instability; balanced_mix if two or more of these levels are equally foregrounded."
            }
          ]
        },
        "conflict_and_opposition": {
          "aspect_name": "Conflict Type and Outcome",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_CON_001",
              "name": "Primary Conflict Locus",
              "question": "Is the central conflict primarily internal to a character, external, or equally both?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "internal",
                "external",
                "balanced_internal_external"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Ask whether the main tension is about a character's inner struggle (guilt, identity), external forces (villains, disasters), or if the plot gives roughly equal weight to both.",
              "merged_from": [
                "AGENT_ROLE_022"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_CON_004",
              "name": "Antagonist Ontology",
              "question": "What best describes the main opposing force in the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_individual_antagonist",
                "multiple_individual_antagonists",
                "impersonal_system_or_institution",
                "impersonal_environment_or_disaster",
                "internal_psychological_conflict",
                "supernatural_or_cosmic_force"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Determine what the protagonist is primarily up against across the whole arc: a particular person, a group, a system, an environment, their own mind, or a cosmic/supernatural entity."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_CON_007",
              "name": "Agency in Resolution",
              "question": "Is the resolution of the central conflict driven mainly by the protagonist's deliberate choices or by events beyond their control?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "primarily_protagonist_choice",
                "mixed_choice_and_chance",
                "primarily_external_fate/chance"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess who or what triggers the turning point: the protagonist's decisions and actions, a combination, or mostly accidents, prophecies, or external interventions."
            }
          ]
        },
        "conflict": {
          "aspect_name": "Conflict and Stakes",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_CON_002",
              "name": "Core Conflict Types",
              "question": "Which classic conflict dyads are instantiated as major drivers of the plot?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "person_vs_person",
                "person_vs_society",
                "person_vs_nature",
                "person_vs_self",
                "person_vs_supernatural_or_tech",
                "person_vs_fate_or_time"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Map protagonist(s) against their principal opposition. Select all that apply when that dyad significantly shapes the action: someone contending with another character (vs_person), with collective norms or institutions (vs_society), with environment or animals (vs_nature), with their own impulses or trauma (vs_self), with gods, magic, AI, or devices (vs_supernatural_or_tech), or with inevitabilities like mortality, prophecy, or branching timelines (vs_fate_or_time)."
            }
          ]
        },
        "conflict_and_stakes": {
          "aspect_name": "Conflict and Stakes",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_CON_003",
              "name": "Stakes Domains at Risk",
              "question": "Which domains are significantly at stake in the central conflict?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "physical_survival_or_bodily_harm",
                "personal_relationships_and_family",
                "social_or_political_order",
                "identity_or_psychological_integrity",
                "moral_or_spiritual_salvation",
                "cosmic_or_existential_meaning"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Note explicit threats and possible consequences mentioned or implied. Mark each domain where loss or change would have serious narrative weight: death/injury, destruction of relationships, collapse or corruption of institutions, breakdown of self, damnation/redemption stakes, or the meaning/continuity of reality itself.",
              "merged_from": [
                "EVT_TYP_007"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "structural_arc_form": {
          "aspect_name": "Structural Arc Form",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_001",
              "name": "Global Arc Shape",
              "question": "What overall structural shape does the plot follow?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "classic_rising_action_to_climax_to_denouement",
                "episodic_or_serial_adventures",
                "circular_or_return_to_start_state",
                "fragmentary_or_elliptical",
                "iterative_or_variation_on_a_scenario",
                "deliberately_flat_or_anti_climactic"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Chart tension and event progression across the story. Identify whether it builds toward a single high point then resolves; moves through loosely connected episodes; ends where it began; jumps between disjointed fragments; repeats variations on a scenario (e.g., multiple executions); or intentionally avoids peaks and resolutions."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_002",
              "name": "Narrative Entry Frame",
              "question": "How does the story enter its timeline with respect to the main events?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "chronological_from_earliest_relevant_event",
                "in_medias_res_with_backstory_revealed_later",
                "framed_or_retrospective_narration"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look at the opening: does it begin at the start of the causal chain, drop into the middle and later fill gaps via flashback, or present the whole as a story told from a later vantage point (letters, confession, older narrator looking back)?"
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_003",
              "name": "Density of Subplots",
              "question": "How many substantive subplots or secondary arcs interweave with the main plot?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "no_significant_subplots",
                "one_or_two_minor_subplots",
                "multiple_interwoven_subplots_or_ensemble_arcs"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify additional narrative threads with their own goals and turns (e.g., side romances, institutional reforms, parallel investigations). Count only those developed over multiple scenes. Judge whether there are none, a couple of minor ones, or a dense ensemble of interlocking arcs."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_005",
              "name": "Dominant Revelation Pattern",
              "question": "What is the primary pattern by which new information and surprises are delivered?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "mystery_or_investigation_driven",
                "dramatic_irony_reader_knows_more_than_characters",
                "transparent_exposition_minimal_secrets",
                "twist_or_reversal_focused",
                "iterative_reframing_of_the_same_events"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Track how readers learn key facts: through clues and deductions, through privileged access the characters lack, through straightforward exposition with few withheld secrets, via sudden late reversals, or by revisiting the same scenario in multiple versions that alter its meaning.",
              "merged_from": [
                "PLT_STR_012"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_006",
              "name": "Climax Placement",
              "question": "Where, structurally, does the main climactic moment occur in the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "late_climax_near_end",
                "central_climax_mid_story",
                "multiple_climactic_peaks",
                "no_clear_climactic_peak"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Plot the point of maximum tension or decisive change. See if it falls in the final fifth of the text, around the middle, occurs in several comparable surges, or is intentionally diffuse such that no single scene stands as a clear climax."
            }
          ]
        },
        "moral_and_closure": {
          "aspect_name": "Moral Stance and Closure",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_001",
              "name": "Moral/Lesson Explicitness",
              "question": "How overtly does the story articulate a moral, lesson, or prescriptive takeaway?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "no_discernible_moral_or_thematic_judgment",
                "implicit_moral_inferred_from_outcomes_and_tone",
                "explicit_didactic_moral_or_authorial_comment"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for explicit generalized statements about how one ought to live or what the story 'means.' If absent, but outcomes clearly reward or punish behaviors in a patterned way, mark implicit. If the narrator or characters plainly state the lesson, mark explicit_didactic_moral_or_authorial_comment."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_003",
              "name": "Ending Closure Type",
              "question": "What kind of closure does the ending provide for plot and character arcs?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "closed_resolution_plot_and_fates_mostly_settled",
                "open_ending_major_plot_threads_unresolved",
                "ambiguous_or_interpretive_ending",
                "cyclical_return_to_beginning_motif",
                "cliffhanger_designed_to_lead_into_sequel"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Examine the final scenes: are main conflicts resolved with futures sketched, or are big questions left hanging? Is the last note interpretively puzzling rather than event-focused? Does the story end by echoing its beginning, or by suspending action at a precarious moment clearly meant to continue?"
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_004",
              "name": "Protagonist Transformational Trajectory",
              "question": "How does the primary protagonist change internally over the course of the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "positive_growth_or_enlightenment",
                "negative_fall_or_corruption",
                "mixed_or_partial_change",
                "no_significant_internal_change"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Compare the protagonist's beliefs, self-understanding, and habitual choices at start and end. Determine whether they gain insight or maturity, deteriorate morally/psychologically, experience a conflicted or incomplete shift, or remain essentially the same despite events.",
              "merged_from": [
                "AGENT_ATTR_007",
                "AGENT_MOT_015",
                "AGENT_ATTR_020"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_006",
              "name": "Degree of Closure",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how fully does the ending close down narrative questions and conflicts?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Rate 1 if many central issues remain undecided; 3 if some threads are resolved and others left; 5 if almost all major plot questions receive definite answers."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_007",
              "name": "Post-Climax Denouement Length",
              "question": "How extended is the narrative after the main climactic event?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "none_or_minimal (story ends immediately after climax)",
                "brief (a short scene or paragraph of aftermath)",
                "extended (multiple scenes/time jumps of aftermath/epilogue)"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Locate the main climax, then count how much textual space follows. Classify as immediate cutoff, quick wrap-up, or substantial epilogue/after-story."
            }
          ]
        },
        "moral": {
          "aspect_name": "Moral and Ethical Framing",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_MOR_002",
              "name": "Moral Polarity Toward Protagonist",
              "question": "What evaluative stance does the narrative ultimately take toward its central protagonist?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "affirmative_heroic",
                "critical_tragic_flaw",
                "ambivalent_or_morally_mixed",
                "subversive_or_antiheroic"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Combine narrator commentary, plot consequences, and other characters' responses. If the protagonist's actions are framed as admirable and largely vindicated, mark affirmative_heroic. If they are sympathetically portrayed but ultimately condemned or destroyed by their own flaw, mark critical_tragic_flaw. If the story neither clearly endorses nor condemns them, or presents a complex blend, mark ambivalent_or_morally_mixed. If the narrative invites readers to side with someone conventionally villainous or to question all moral frames, mark subversive_or_antiheroic."
            }
          ]
        },
        "arc_and_temporal_structure": {
          "aspect_name": "Arc Shape and Temporal Structure",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_007",
              "name": "Tension Escalation Clarity",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how clearly does the story build and escalate narrative tension toward one or more climaxes?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Rate 1 if stakes feel flat or random, 3 if there is some build but with muddled signposting, 5 if each sequence clearly raises stakes/complication toward a focused climax."
            }
          ]
        },
        "stakes_and_scope": {
          "aspect_name": "Stakes and Consequences",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_009",
              "name": "Primary Stakes Domain",
              "question": "What is primarily at stake in the central conflict?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "physical_survival/bodily_harm",
                "relationships/love/family",
                "identity/sanity/psychic_integrity",
                "social_order/community/institutions",
                "cosmic/metaphysical_order",
                "material_gain/reputation"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Ask what the protagonist stands to lose most critically if they fail: life/health, a relationship, their sense of self, the stability of a community/order, the cosmos, or wealth/status."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_010",
              "name": "Stakes Breadth",
              "question": "How broad are the consequences of failure or success in the central conflict?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "intimate (affects only protagonist or small dyad)",
                "local (affects a family, team, or small community)",
                "societal (affects a city, nation, or large institution)",
                "global_or_cosmic (worldwide, planetary, or metaphysical stakes)"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Determine the largest group meaningfully impacted by the outcome: just the main character, a small circle, a wider society, or the world/cosmos."
            },
            {
              "id": "PLT_STR_011",
              "name": "Stakes Types Present",
              "question": "Which types of stakes are meaningfully in play?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "physical_survival",
                "emotional/relational_loss",
                "moral_or_spiritual_integrity",
                "social_status/reputation",
                "economic/security",
                "knowledge/truth/reality_stability",
                "ecological/planetary_health"
              ],
              "detection_method": "For each category, ask whether losing it would count as a major consequence portrayed in the story (e.g., risk of death, betrayal, moral corruption, public disgrace, poverty, loss of truth, environmental ruin). Select all that apply."
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    "setting": {
      "dimension_name": "Setting",
      "dimension_description": "Where and when: locations, time, atmosphere, world-building, spatial imagination",
      "aspects": {
        "spatial_specificity_and_scope": {
          "aspect_name": "Spatial Specificity and Scope",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_005",
              "name": "Dominant Spatial Scale",
              "question": "What is the dominant spatial scale of the story's core action?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "intimate_or_bodily",
                "household_or_local_block",
                "urban_or_regional",
                "planetary_or_cosmic",
                "multi_scale_mixed"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify where most crucial scenes unfold. If they focus on a bed, a table, or a single room, select intimate_or_bodily. If they mostly span a house, yard, or immediate neighborhood, select household_or_local_block. If city-wide movement and civic spaces dominate, select urban_or_regional. If entire planets, oceans, or space are the main arenas, select planetary_or_cosmic. If the story regularly shifts meaningfully across two or more scales (e.g., kitchen to global network to starship), select multi_scale_mixed.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_LOC_006"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_008",
              "name": "Dominant Space Types",
              "question": "Which types of spaces dominate the story's significant scenes?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "domestic_private",
                "public_social",
                "natural_outdoor",
                "institutional_or_workplace",
                "virtual_or_digital"
              ],
              "detection_method": "For each scene, note the type of space (home interiors, streets/bars/fairs, forests/rivers, schools/hospitals/offices, online environments). Tally which types recur most as settings for key events. Select up to two categories that best capture the dominant arenas."
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_009",
              "name": "Recurring Symbolic Anchor Settings",
              "question": "Does the story repeatedly return to one or two key locations that function as symbolic anchors for its themes?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "yes",
                "no"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for places revisited multiple times at emotionally pivotal moments (a holy tree, a cellar, a bridge, a greenhouse). If such locations recur and clearly gather symbolic or thematic weight beyond convenience, choose yes. If settings change frequently without such symbolic reuse, choose no."
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_010",
              "name": "Ontological Ambiguity of Place",
              "question": "How straightforwardly real vs ontologically unstable is the setting presented as being within the story?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "straightforward_mimetic",
                "mildly_unreliable_or_magical",
                "strongly_ambiguous_or_simulated"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess whether the text invites you to read the world as continuous with everyday reality, or whether it questions its own reality (dreams, simulations, loops). If there is no suggestion of unreliability or non-natural forces affecting the fabric of place, select straightforward_mimetic. If there are clear magical/supernatural elements but the world's reality is not itself in doubt, select mildly_unreliable_or_magical. If the narrative repeatedly hints that the setting is a simulation, dream, experiment, or otherwise ontologically unstable (Big Box loops, Flux, multiverses treated as uncertain), select strongly_ambiguous_or_simulated."
            }
          ]
        },
        "spatial_specificity_and_scale": {
          "aspect_name": "Spatial Specificity and Scale",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_002",
              "name": "Spatial Granularity Level",
              "question": "How fine-grained is the story's depiction of physical space and geography?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "1_very_low",
                "2_low",
                "3_medium",
                "4_high"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess the density and precision of spatial markers: number of distinct place names, room names, street names, and micro-locational cues. Very low: almost no concrete location detail. Low: a few coarse labels (house, city). Medium: recurring named rooms/streets with some layout hints. High: map-like inventories of spaces, routes, and relative positions.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_LOC_001"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_011",
              "name": "Location Variety Scope",
              "question": "How many distinct physical locales does the story meaningfully inhabit over its course?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "1_single_primary_location",
                "2_two_to_four_locales",
                "3_many_within_one_region",
                "4_multi_regional_or_international",
                "5_multiworld_or_multiverse"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Count distinct settings that host full scenes (not just mentioned in passing). Single cottage or lab = 1. A house plus a school and one bar = 2\u20134. Numerous neighborhoods within the same city/valley = 3. Travel between cities/countries = 4. Regular shifts between planets, dimensions, or branched realities = 5."
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_016",
              "name": "Ontological Stability of Environment",
              "question": "Does the setting obey stable, realist physics, or does it feature magical, speculative, or reality-fluid properties?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "realist_stable",
                "realist_with_magical_intrusions",
                "fully_speculative_but_rule_based",
                "reality_fluid_or_unstable"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Check whether the story's world appears to follow ordinary physical laws without comment (realist_stable); is recognizably our world but with occasional overt magic/hauntings/portals (realist_with_magical_intrusions); is an invented SF/fantasy world with consistent alternative rules and technologies (fully_speculative_but_rule_based); or repeatedly undermines spatial/temporal continuity (loops, shifting architecture, simulation resets) so that 'reality' itself is unstable."
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_018",
              "name": "Setting Mobility Pattern",
              "question": "How does the protagonist's relationship to place evolve structurally: mostly static, a one-way journey, a back-and-forth oscillation, or a return home transformed?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "static_single_hub",
                "outward_journey_only",
                "pendulum_home_away",
                "spiral_departure_and_return"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Outline the sequence of major settings. Static_single_hub: nearly all action stays in one primary locale. Outward_journey_only: the story steadily moves away from the starting point without returning. Pendulum_home_away: repeated departures and returns between a home base and other sites. Spiral_departure_and_return: an arc that ends back at or near the starting place, but with changed circumstances or perception."
            }
          ]
        },
        "spatial_specificity_and_ontology": {
          "aspect_name": "Spatial Specificity and Ontology",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_003",
              "name": "Geospatial Coherence",
              "question": "How coherently mapped is the story's geography across its locations?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_coherent_region",
                "multiple_regions_with_clear_map",
                "collage_of_unconnected_locales",
                "deliberately_fluid_or_shifting_geography"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess whether scenes all occur in one clearly understood area; in several regions with explicit spatial relations; as a series of largely unconnected backdrops; or in spaces whose layout is intentionally unstable, shifting, or impossible."
            }
          ]
        },
        "setting_introduction_and_anchoring": {
          "aspect_name": "Setting Introduction and Spatial Anchoring",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_004",
              "name": "Opening Spatial Grounding",
              "question": "How clearly does the story's opening ground the reader in a specific physical setting?",

              "values": [
                "none_or_very_vague",
                "minimal_local_details_only",
                "clear_local_setting_but_limited_global_context",
                "clear_local_and_global_spatial_context"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Examine the first scene: note whether it gives no concrete location, only a room or generic area, a specific place without wider context, or both local scene and its position in a larger geography (e.g. city, country)."

          ]
        },
        "scale_and_spatial_mobility": {
          "aspect_name": "Scale and Spatial Mobility",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_007",
              "name": "Spatial Mobility Pattern",
              "question": "How much does the narrative move between distinct locations?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "single_primary_location",
                "multiple_locations_within_one_area",
                "travel_between_distant_regions_or_worlds"
              ],
              "detection_method": "List all distinct settings visited; assess whether action stays rooted in one site, shifts among several nearby sites (same town/city/ship), or features significant journeys between far-separated places or realms."
            }
          ]
        },
        "space_types_and_ecology": {
          "aspect_name": "Types of Spaces and Spatial Ecology",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_012",
              "name": "Built vs Natural Setting Balance",
              "question": "What is the balance between built (human-made) and natural environments in the story's settings?",

              "values": [
                "mostly_indoor_built_environments",
                "mixed_built_and_natural",
                "mostly_outdoor_natural_environments"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Estimate whether the majority of scenes occur inside buildings and urban structures; are split relatively evenly between constructed and outdoor natural spaces; or are predominantly in landscapes, wilderness, or minimally built environments."
            }
          ]
        },
        "worldbuilding_and_infrastructure": {
          "aspect_name": "World-Building and Infrastructure",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_013",
              "name": "Speculative World-Building Depth",
              "question": "For speculative or non-mimetic settings, how deeply does the story elaborate systemic aspects of its world (technology, social orders, ecologies, metaphysics)?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "In SF/fantasy/horror tales, tally how many concrete systems are sketched (political structures, economic rules, magic or tech constraints, ecology, history). If the speculative element is a single vague premise with little surrounding detail, score 1. If several systems are present but only lightly touched, score 3. If multiple interlocking systems are richly described and clearly shape daily life and events (Atlantis, Darkling grain networks, Arbor Fortuna), score 5.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_ATM_010",
                "SIT_GEN_007"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_LOC_014",
              "name": "Environmental and Ecological Emphasis",
              "question": "To what extent does the story foreground landscape, climate, and ecological processes as part of the setting's logic?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for passages about rivers, forests, farms, weather patterns, dust, blight, floods, animals, or resource cycles that go beyond mere backdrop. If environment is scarcely described, score 1. If natural features occasionally shape mood or minor events, score 3. If ecological systems are central\u2014villages eaten by jungle, grain-law deserts, derbies in wheat oceans\u2014score 5."
            }
          ]
        },
        "temporal_structure": {
          "aspect_name": "Temporal Setting and Structure",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_TIM_015",
              "name": "Temporal Setting Specificity",
              "question": "How specifically is the time period of the story identified or implied?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "timeless_or_mythic",
                "implied_period_only",
                "explicit_historical_past",
                "contemporary_realistic",
                "near_future_speculative",
                "far_future_or_deep_time"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Check for explicit dates, wars, technologies, or historical events. If time is never indicated and feels fairy-tale or mythic, choose timeless_or_mythic. If clues suggest a general era (Victorian, 1950s) but no specific dates, choose implied_period_only. If real historical periods are clearly anchored (Omaha Beach, 11th-century Normandy), choose explicit_historical_past. If the setting feels like our present, choose contemporary_realistic. If there are small extrapolations (near-future tech, minor societal changes), choose near_future_speculative. If the narrative is set in starship eras, post-human futures, or geological epochs, choose far_future_or_deep_time.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_TIM_001"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_TIM_016",
              "name": "Temporal Scaffolding Complexity",
              "question": "How complex is the story's handling of time (flashbacks, jumps, parallel timelines)?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Map the story's chronology. If events are told in straightforward linear order in a single time frame, score 1. If there are a few simple flashbacks or a frame narrative, score 3. If the story frequently moves across eras, uses Rashomon-like retellings, counterfactual branches, or elaborate frames (war stories framed by convent years later, multi-decade cryo), score 5, with intermediate values for moderate complexity."
            }
          ]
        },
        "sensory_texture": {

          "features": [

Select all modalities that appear regularly and distinctly in setting description, not just once or twice in passing.",
              "merged_from": [
