        "atmosphere_and_symbolism": {
          "aspect_name": "Atmosphere, Mood, and Symbolic Use of Setting",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_019",
              "name": "Setting\u2013Plot Causal Role",
              "question": "What best describes the relationship between setting and plot causality?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "backdrop_only",
                "constraints_and_obstacles",
                "active_agent_or_antagonist",
                "structuring_symbolic_landscape"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Ask: could the same story unfold in a very different place with minimal changes? If yes, choose backdrop_only. If terrain, weather, lay-out, or social geography regularly create concrete obstacles or affordances (escape routes, sieges, floods), choose constraints_and_obstacles. If the environment itself acts like a quasi-character\u2014blight that consumes villages, sentient grain-law, Flux, Gorge Entity\u2014choose active_agent_or_antagonist. If locations are arranged to mirror inner journeys or moral structures (sequential stations, ascents/descents) more than literal causality, choose structuring_symbolic_landscape.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_ATM_009"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_020",
              "name": "Atmospheric Construction Techniques",
              "question": "Which elements does the story most rely on to build atmosphere and mood in its settings?",
              "type": "multi_select",
              "values": [
                "weather_and_light",
                "architecture_and_objects",
                "nature_and_landscape",
                "crowds_and_noise",
                "decay_and_dirt",
                "technology_and_media"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Identify recurring tools for mood: storms, heatwaves, fog, dusk (weather_and_light); detailed interiors, furniture, machines (architecture_and_objects); rivers, forests, cliffs (nature_and_landscape); busy streets, chanting crowds (crowds_and_noise); dust, rot, grime (decay_and_dirt); screens, ads, loudspeakers, data-streams (technology_and_media). Select all that are central to how the prose creates atmosphere, not just incidentally present.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_ATM_012"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_022",
              "name": "Setting as Psychological Mirror",
              "question": "To what degree does the story use physical environment as a mirror or metaphor for characters' inner states?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for explicit or implicit correlations between mood and place (dust as shroud of grief, collapsing houses as failing marriages, blight as guilt). If settings and emotions rarely echo each other, score 1. If some key scenes align weather/landscape/architecture with emotional turns, but many do not, score 3. If the story consistently externalizes psychology through place and repeatedly aligns environmental change with inner change, score 5.",
              "merged_from": [
                "SET_ATM_014"
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "setting_plot_relationship": {
          "aspect_name": "Setting\u2013Plot Relationship",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_003",
              "name": "Setting Agency Level",
              "question": "To what extent does the setting itself act as an agentive force affecting the plot?",

            }
          ]
        },

          "aspect_name": "Atmosphere and Mood",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_004",
              "name": "Dominant Setting Mood Qualities",

        "sensory_and_atmospheric_texture": {
          "aspect_name": "Sensory and Atmospheric Texture",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "SET_ATM_005",
              "name": "Sensory Density",
              "question": "How dense is the sensory description of the setting across the narrative?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [

                "2_sparse",
                "3_moderate",
                "4_rich",
                "5_lush_overdetermined"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Estimate the proportion of sentences devoted to sensory detail and the layering of multiple senses per scene. Minimal: mostly abstract summary or dialogue with almost no concrete description. Sparse: occasional brief scene-setting. Moderate: regular but unobtrusive descriptive lines. Rich: most scenes include multi-sensory description. Lush_overdetermined: descriptions are frequent, extended, and highly sensuous, often slowing pace.",

              "name": "Dominant Environmental Mood",

              "values": [

                "cozy_or_idyllic",
                "bleak_or_desolate",
                "uncanny_or_haunted",
                "wondrous_or_sublime",
                "satirical_or_grotesque"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Aggregate the emotional valence of recurring setting descriptions: neutral everyday detail (mundane_realist), warmth/safety/comfort (cozy_or_idyllic), emptiness, decay, or oppression (bleak_or_desolate), strangeness and dread (uncanny_or_haunted), awe and grandeur (wondrous_or_sublime), or exaggerated, mocking, or carnival-like distortion (satirical_or_grotesque).               "merged_from": [

          "features": [

    "style": {
      "dimension_name": "Style",
      "dimension_description": "Language: figurative language, sentence structure, register, tone, allusion, prose texture",
      "aspects": {
        "figurative_devices": {
          "aspect_name": "Figurative Devices and Tropes",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_001",
              "name": "Figurative Device Density",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how densely does the passage use figurative language such as metaphor, simile, or personification relative to its length?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1",
                "2",
                "3",
                "4",
                "5"
              ],
              "detection_method": "In a representative 200\u2013400 word span, count or estimate how many sentences or main clauses contain clear figurative language, then assign 1 (almost none) to 5 (multiple tropes per sentence)."
            },
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_002",
              "name": "Dominant Figurative Device Type",
              "question": "Which figurative device type is most frequently used in the passage?",
              "type": "categorical",
              "values": [
                "mostly_literal (no clear dominant trope)",
                "simile_dominant",
                "metaphor_dominant",
                "personification_or_prosopopoeia_dominant",
                "mixed_no_clear_dominant"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Scan for simile markers (like, as if), implicit metaphors, and personifying uses of nonhuman subjects; judge which device appears most often relative to the others."
            }
          ]
        },
        "figurative_intensity": {
          "aspect_name": "Figurative intensity and devices",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_003",
              "name": "Conventional vs fresh figurative language",
              "question": "How original versus conventional are the figurative expressions overall?",
              "type": "ordinal",
              "values": [
                "1 - mostly_clich\u00e9d_or_stock_phrases",
                "2 - mix_of_clich\u00e9_and_some_fresh_images",
                "3 - predominantly_fresh_and_inventive_images"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Compare key figurative phrases to common idioms; judge whether wording feels familiar and formulaic or surprising and idiosyncratic."
            },
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_004",
              "name": "Presence of extended conceit",
              "question": "Does the passage develop an extended, multi-step metaphor or conceit sustained over several sentences?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "absent",
                "present"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Look for a single comparison or image that is elaborated through multiple clauses or sentences (e.g., a city as a body or war as a disease) rather than one-off figures.",
              "merged_from": [
                "STY_FIG_006"
              ]
            },
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_005",
              "name": "Recurrent metaphorical motif",
              "question": "Does the passage use a recurring metaphorical motif (e.g., weight, music, machinery) that structures multiple images?",
              "type": "binary",
              "values": [
                "absent",
                "present"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Scan figurative language for repeated source domains (such as legal, musical, religious, or ecological imagery) that recur across the passage and link different elements."
            }
          ]
        },
        "imagery_sensory": {
          "aspect_name": "Imagery and sensory grounding",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_007",
              "name": "Overall imageability",
              "question": "How vividly and concretely can a reader visualize or sensorially imagine this passage?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1 - very_low_imageability_mostly_abstract",
                "2 - low_imageability_with_sporadic_concrete_detail",
                "3 - moderate_imageability",
                "4 - high_imageability_rich_concrete_detail",
                "5 - extremely_vivid_and_sensorially_dense"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Assess the proportion and specificity of concrete nouns, modifiers, and sensory verbs; judge how easily a detailed mental scene forms."
            },
            {
              "id": "STY_FIG_009",
              "name": "Concrete vs abstract lexis balance",
              "question": "On a 1\u20135 scale, how much does the passage favor concrete, physical vocabulary versus abstract, conceptual vocabulary?",
              "type": "scale",
              "values": [
                "1 - predominantly_abstract_terms",
                "2 - mostly_abstract_with_some_concrete",
                "3 - balanced_mix_of_concrete_and_abstract",
                "4 - mostly_concrete_with_some_abstract",
                "5 - overwhelmingly_concrete_and_thing-focused"
              ],
              "detection_method": "Sample ~100\u2013150 content words and judge the proportion that denote tangible entities and actions versus ideas, mental states, or generalized qualities."
            }
          ]
        },
        "syntax_and_structure": {
          "aspect_name": "Syntax and Structural Complexity",
          "features": [
            {
              "id": "STY_CPX_002",
              "name": "Predominant Sentence Length Band",
